sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:2696
Court No. - 9

Case :- Matters Under Article 227 No. - 14840 of 2024
Petitioner :- National Highways Authority Of India

Respondent :- Additional Commissioner Admn And 7 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Anurag Yadav

Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Deepak Singh,Harish Chandra Singh
Hon'ble Rohit Ranjan Agarwal,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit, filed today, is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Anurag Yadav, learned counsel for petitioner, learned Standing Counsel for respondent no. 1 and 2 and Sri Harish Chandra Singh, learned counsel for respondent nos. 3 to 8.
3.

Through this writ petition, a challenge has been laid to order dated 05.10.2024 passed by Additional District Judge, Court No. 1, Firozabad in Arbitration Case No. 45 of 2021 partly rejecting the application moved by petitioner for amending the application moved under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (hereinafter called as "the Act of 1996").

sentences.text: Facts, leading to filing of the the writ petition, are that petitioner that is National Highways Authority of India (in short "NHAI") had acquired certain piece of land for construction of road widening of Agra-Etawah Bypass Road Section in District Firozabad.
A notification under Section 3A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 (hereinafter called as "the Act of 1956") was issued in the year 2018.

Subsequently, the land was acquired and the award was made under the Right to Fare Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 on 03.05.2019 under Section 3G(1) of the Act of 1956.

entities.text: Right to Fare Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereafter, contesting respondents no. 3 to 8 had filed an application for enhancement of compensation under Section 3G(5) of the Act.
Additional Commissioner, Agra Division, Agra was appointed as Arbitrator who made an award on 13.03.2020.
Aggrieved by the said award, petitioner had moved an application under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 before District Judge, Firozabad.
According to petitioner, in para no. 10, typing error had occurred in place of "Agra Division, Agra", "Kanpur Division, Kanpur" was transcribed.

Further,
other amendments were also sought through the application.

By order impugned, the court below has rejected the amendment application to the extent that the words "Agra Division, Agra" in place of "Kanpur Division, Kanpur" has been refused to be amended while the other amendment as sought by petitioner has been allowed.

5. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that it was a typographical error and as the award was made by Arbitrator i.e. Additional Commissioner, Administration, Agra, the amendment should have been allowed by court below.

6. Sri Singh, learned counsel appearing for claimants-respondents had vehemently opposed the writ petition and submitted that provision of Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is specifically barred under Section 19 of the Act and court below had rightly refused to amend the words "Agra Division, Agra"
in place of "Kanpur Division, Kanpur".
7.
I have heard respective counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.

8. It is an admitted fact to both the parties that the award was made by Additional Commissioner,
Administration, Agra Division, Agra while exercising jurisdiction under Section 3G(5).
The order under challenge before District Judge in proceedings under Section 34 of the Act of 1996 is as to the award made in proceedings under Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956.

The sole ground on which the claimants-respondents had opposed the amendment is that correspondence between the counsel who had appeared on behalf of NHAI had addressed his letter that Additional Commissioner,
Kanpur Division, Kanpur had made an award under Section 3G(5) and, as such, the amendment should not have been allowed.

I find that it was a communication between the counsel of petitioner inter se which could not determine the ground of amendment in the application moved under Section 34 and court below should have allowed the same as the award which is on record clearly demonstrates that it was made by Additional Commissioner, Administration, Agra Division, Agra and not by Additional Commissioner, Kanpur Division, Kanpur.

Further, Section 19 of the Act of 1996 only postulates that the Arbitration Tribunal shall not be bound of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 or the Indian Evidence Act and it does not restrict the application of Code of Civil Procedure.

Once the court below had partly allowed the amendment application, it should have given due consideration to the fact that award under 3G(5) was made by Additional Commissioner,

2

entities.text:
Additional Commissioner,
National Highways Authority Of India vs Additional Commissioner Admn And 7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Administration, Agra and amendment application should have been allowed.
Further, Reliance placed by respondents counsel on the various decisions of Bombay High Court and Madras High Court are distinguishable on the facts of the present case.
9. In view of said fact, the writ petition succeeds and is allowed.

10. The order dated 05.10.2024 passed by Additional District Judge, Court No. 1, Firozabad is set aside and amendment application moved by petitioner stands allowed and due amendment shall be carried out by petitioner in his application under Section 34 of Act of 1996, within a period of 15 days from today.
